newsitem.title: USA: Jury begins deliberations in Reynolds tobacco trial.
newsitem.headline: Jury begins deliberations in Reynolds tobacco trial.

text.p: Jurors began deliberating Friday afternoon in the trial of a wrongful death lawsuit against R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co.

The five-woman, one-man panel heard more than five hours of closing arguments from the two sides before retiring to consider whether Reynolds was negligent in the death of smoker Jean Connor, who died in October 1995 of lung cancer.
The jury also will be asked to decide whether Reynolds, a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp., manufactured a defective and dangerous product that contributed to Connor's death.
Reynolds was sued by the family of Connor, who began smoking Reynolds' Salem brand cigarettes as a teenager.

Judge Bernard Nachman said he might allow the jury to halt deliberations for the weekend around 7 p.m. EDT unless they felt they were close to a verdict. Jurors had earlier indicated they were not willing to deliberate Saturday.

In closing arguments, Reynolds reiterated its claim that Connor had chosen to smoke despite "vast" public knowledge of the potential health risks. Attorneys for plaintiff Dana Raulerson, Connor's sister, countered that the company had a duty to warn the public even if such knowledge was widespread.
